notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. LEADER: the proxy says Henrique Braun succeeded James Quincey as CEO effective March 31, 2026 and Quincey continues as Executive Chairman of the Board, so relation is now 'chair'. Quincey beneficially owns 4,461,496 shares, less than 1% (marked * in the proxy), so pctEconomic is null; the figure includes 3,879,031 shares under options exercisable by May 1, 2026 and excludes 35,443 cash-settled Supplemental 401(k) share units. 5% HOLDERS: Berkshire's 9.29% reflects what it told the company as of December 31, 2025; Vanguard's and BlackRock's still rest on Schedule 13G/As reporting holdings at the end of 2023, and the proxy computes all three percentages on the assumption the holders still owned those shares on March 2, 2026 (proxy footnote 4). DIVIDENDS: the cash-flow line is dividends to Coca-Cola shareowners ($8,779m, matching the equity statement). GEOGRAPHY: the 10-K's own United States / International geographic data; the operating segments are not used.

economicActivity.label: Coca-Cola system economic activity
economicActivity.definition: Modeled contribution to GDP (value added) of The Coca-Cola Company plus its independent U.S. bottlers ("the Coca-Cola system"), including suppliers, distributors, retailers and re-spending of wages, from a Multi-Regional Input-Output model by consultancy Steward Redqueen. Published rounded ($2B, $443M); values in millions are converted to billions in the bracketed note.

jobsSupported.label: Jobs supported by the Coca-Cola system
jobsSupported.definition: Direct, supplier, value-chain and induced jobs the Coca-Cola system supports in the state, modeled by Steward Redqueen; published rounded as "23K+".

directEmployees.label: Direct Coca-Cola system employees
directEmployees.definition: Direct employees of The Coca-Cola Company and its independent bottlers in the state, per the study; published rounded as "3K+". Most are bottler employees, not TCCC employees.

footprint.notes: State rows come from The Coca-Cola Company's U.S. Economic & Community Impact map (company-hosted table for 50 states, DC, Puerto Rico and cities), a study by consultancy Steward Redqueen ("Steward Redqueen 2026 Assessment"; "reflective of the calendar year 2025"), so tier is company-commissioned. No newer edition found (checked Nov 24, 2026): the live map still shows the same figures for all 51 rows. The study attribution and the 'calendar year 2025' wording are carried over from the earlier fetch; they are not in the HTML served on Nov 24, 2026, which holds only the table. An earlier Steward Redqueen study covered 2022 ($57.8B nationally, press release Sept 2023), but its state figures are no longer published. All state figures cover the whole Coca-Cola system (TCCC plus independent bottlers), not the company alone, and are rounded by the source; Puerto Rico and city rows are left out; goods-and-services purchased and community investment columns not recorded. Regions: the FY2025 10-K facility table by operating segment (Dec 31, 2025); only the four geographic segments are recorded (the 10-K now labels the first one 'EMEA'). Bottling Investments (56 owned and 5 leased bottling plants) and Corporate are not geographic and are left out; the FY2025 table no longer has a Global Ventures row, and its 1,379 leased retail stores now sit in the EMEA row; distribution, storage and retail columns are not recorded. U.S. company employees approximately 8,900 of ~65,900 total at Dec 31, 2025 (10-K; the decrease is attributed to 2025 divestitures). No employees-by-state or taxes-by-country found.

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Operating cash flow is again depressed by working capital (net change in operating assets and liabilities −7,208), so the single-year figure is high relative to a normal year. Acquisitions of businesses and equity investments (461) excluded. Cash taxes paid come from the new by-jurisdiction table in the income-tax note (ASU 2023-09, adopted prospectively); no XBRL fact was found for it at the new year end.

CalPERS: the source is the information table of CalPERS's Form 13F for the quarter ended September 30, 2026; Form 13F covers only U.S.-listed securities, and the quoted row gives issuer, class, CUSIP, value in dollars and shares (a separate row for Coca-Cola Consolidated, a different company, is not counted). The CalPERS percentage divides its September 30, 2026 shares by the 10-Q cover count at October 26, 2026, the same count used in the marketcap lens. pay.notes: Employees: approximate year-end count from the FY2025 10-K; the drop from about 69,700 is mainly 2025 divestitures. Payroll: the 10-K gives no total of salaries, benefits or personnel costs, so the proxy's CEO pay ratio median for 2025 (same year as the head count) is used. Most employees are outside the United States (about 8,900 are U.S.-based), and the median is converted to U.S. dollars, which is why it is low.
